evidence.text: 漢典 describes ancient 二 as a primitive counting sign represented by two horizontal strokes. It cites classical-text usages for the numeral and gives Du Fu’s Tang poem 石壕吏 for an ordinal ‘second’ use; it also cites 左傳 for 二心, ‘divided or disloyal heart.’ These are dictionary quotations, not independently dated manuscript witnesses, and do not establish the paths or earliest dates of the extensions.
evidence.title: 二 èr - 汉典

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 二, transcribed ancient scripts and Chinese pronunciation sections
evidence.field: graphic account, readings, and lexical reconstruction
evidence.text: The entry characterizes 二 as an ideogram formed from two parallel strokes and lists standard Mandarin èr (Pinyin), Guangzhou–Hong Kong Cantonese ji6 (Jyutping), Middle Chinese Baxter nyijH, fanqie 而至切, Zhengzhang Old Chinese *njis (2003), and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ni[j]-s (2014). It also reports a Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison and a proposed alternate coda analysis; these concern the spoken numeral, not the graph’s formation. The page says its ancient forms draw on collections including Shuowen, bronze-inscription compilations, and oracle-bone materials, but does not give a dated earliest 二 inscription in the inspected passage.

evidence.text: This record proposes that 二 resembles two stacked counting rods and notes that early forms have two strokes of equal length, distinguishing them from 上. The page displays bronze inscription and Xiaoxuetang form categories, but its rights footer states All Rights Reserved; it is used here as linked evidence only, not as an image asset.

gaps: No directly dated oracle-bone 二 inscription was verified in this research; earliest attestation and detailed graphic chronology remain open. The selected image documents a mid-Western Zhou bronze-script example via a modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

The Shuowen account associates 二 with earth and paired ones, while later dictionary descriptions characterize it as a counting sign or stacked counting rods. The inspected sources do not independently adjudicate the original formation.
Quoted examples of numeral, ordinal, and figurative uses are not independently dated manuscript witnesses. Earliest dates and precise semantic links remain unestablished.

二 has no meaningful component divisions or phonetic component. Lexical sound reconstructions and comparative proposals concern the spoken numeral and do not change the graphic analysis; underlying comparative arguments were not independently assessed here. No component origin_relation applies.

The Xiaoxuetang oracle-bone landing page did not itself expose a specific 二 oracle-bone record during inspection. chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw states All Rights Reserved, so its glyph images are not proposed for reuse.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw rather than a photograph or scan of the bronze object. The source page links it to 免簋 and a Xiaoxuetang form record, but no artifact image was inspected here.
The ancient graphic sequence and earliest dated attestation remain unverified; this single example should not be read as a complete developmental timeline.
